camera.enable_notes: On some models RTSP and ONVIF are disabled by default and must be enabled in the camera settings. Baichuan-only models (B800/D800, B400/D400, E1, Lumus, 510A) have no RTSP — use the neolink bridge on TCP 9000 instead.

streams.notes: H.264/H.265; 4K on capable models. Force TCP transport in players for reliability.

streams.name: Sub stream (RTSP)
streams.notes: Lower-resolution sub stream for previews / low bandwidth.

methods.notes: Discover via ONVIF WS-Discovery (onvif.yaml) or by probing HTTP /cgi-bin/api.cgi. Confirm with a Login + GetDevInfo. Baichuan-only models are reached by connecting TCP 9000 directly.

device.name: Reolink IP Camera / Doorbell / NVR
device.notes:
Reolink cameras, doorbells and NVRs are locally controllable with the internet fully blocked: they serve an HTTP CGI JSON API, RTSP/RTMP/FLV streams, ONVIF, and a proprietary "Baichuan" binary protocol on TCP 9000. Reolink is active and firmware-updates these, but the vendor app defaults to cloud/UID relay — so a local spec is the rescue for cloud-hesitant owners.
PORTS: HTTP 80, HTTPS 443, RTSP 554, RTMP 1935, ONVIF 8000 (events), TCP 9000 (Baichuan / push events). On some models RTSP/ONVIF must be enabled in the camera settings first.
HTTP CGI API (base http(s)://{ip}/cgi-bin/api.cgi, JSON, driven by a `cmd` param): POST cmd=Login {"User":{"userName":..,"password":..}} returns a token (data.value.Token.name) reused as ?token={token}&cmd={command}. Some units ship admin/123456 until changed.
RTSP: main rtsp://user:pass@{ip}/h264Preview_01_main, sub .../h264Preview_01_sub (or the :554/... form). RTSP carries 4K/H.265; FLV is lightest on the camera.
BAICHUAN (TCP 9000): the only surface on some cameras (B800/D800, B400/D400, E1, Lumus, 510A have no ONVIF/RTSP). Frame: 4-byte LE magic 0x0abcdef0 at offset 0, then messageId (int32 LE @4), messageLen (@8), channel_id (@12), streamID (@13), messageHandle (@15), messageClass (int16 LE @18); header is 20 bytes (legacy) or 24 bytes (modern, encrypt_xml flag @16, binOffset @20). Named message ids: 1 login, 3 Preview (video), 23 Reboot, 80 VersionInfo. XML payloads are XOR-obfuscated with an offset-dependent 8-byte key.

openness.notes: The HTTP CGI / ONVIF / RTSP surface is documented (Reolink's own HTTP API guide); the Baichuan port-9000 protocol is reverse-engineered by neolink. See onvif.yaml for the ONVIF discovery/stream mechanism.

credentials.notes: Local control uses the camera's own admin credential (change the default admin/123456). Onboarding is app-mediated and not documented here.

factory_reset.effect: Clears network config and the admin password, returning the camera to first-boot. Performed by holding the physical reset button; the hold time is model-specific.

procedures.basis: Reolink documents a reset-button hold per model; not replayed here.
procedures.name: Reset button hold

steps.action: Hold the camera's reset button until it reboots into setup.
steps.expect: The camera returns to first-boot state.

methods.description: Onboard the camera onto the network, then (on models where they are off) enable the RTSP and ONVIF ports in the camera settings. Log in locally over /cgi-bin/api.cgi with admin + password.

steps.action: Onboard the camera onto the LAN (app/QR or wired).
Enable RTSP/ONVIF ports in the camera settings if disabled.
steps.expect: RTSP answers on 554 and ONVIF on 8000.

steps.action: Log in over /cgi-bin/api.cgi (cmd=Login) to obtain a token.

setup.notes: The camera joins the LAN (wired or Wi-Fi via the app/QR). On some models RTSP and ONVIF ports must be enabled in the camera UI before RTSP works. Local HTTP login uses admin + a user-set password (some ship admin/123456).

rejoin.notes: Network settings can be changed from the camera UI/app while reachable.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The ports, RTSP URLs, the /cgi-bin/api.cgi login/token flow and the Baichuan (port 9000) header layout are from the Home Assistant integration, reolinkapipy and neolink's dissector.
